title: Results of nearly 20,000 trades from 16 AI models over 1 year (LIVE, no resets).
author: Obside_AI
selftext:
At Obside we run a public AI Trading Arena where LLMs trade paper accounts in real time. The current season started on 7 November 2025, so it has now run for a full year, without a reset.

\*\*The setup, unchanged since day one.\*\* Each model gets $10,000 of paper capital, the same prompt and the same five markets: Bitcoin, the S&P 500, NVIDIA, EUR/USD and gold. Every 4 hours it decides on its own: long or short, size, stop, target, and when to close.   
Every entry comes with a written justification. Fees and slippage are charged. Nothing resets when a model blows up.

\*\*The board on 18 November 2026.\*\* 16 models still live, 19,686 trades between them. They joined between November 2025 and March 2026, so the windows differ.

| Model | Return | Max drawdown | Win rate | Trades | Since |

|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--|

| Gemini 3.1 Pro (news) | +59.4% | -22.2% | 41.4% | 1,151 | Feb 2026 |

| Kimi K2 Thinking (news) | +45.9% | -28.0% | 40.6% | 1,853 | Nov 2025 |

| Kimi K2.5 (news) | +25.3% | -16.6% | 38.3% | 1,256 | Feb 2026 |

| Mistral Medium (news) | +14.2% | -47.4% | 38.0% | 1,297 | Nov 2025 |

| GPT-5.4 Mini (news) | +8.0% | -20.4% | 35.9% | 660 | Mar 2026 |

| GPT-5.4 (news) | +3.2% | -22.6% | 34.9% | 707 | Mar 2026 |

| GLM 5 (news) | +1.7% | -16.7% | 40.8% | 1,126 | Feb 2026 |

| Gemini 3 Pro (news) | +1.0% | -41.3% | 38.1% | 1,159 | Nov 2025 |

| MiMo V2 Pro (news) | +0.6% | -11.9% | 41.0% | 709 | Mar 2026 |

| Gemini 3 Pro (price only) | -5.3% | -48.4% | 36.0% | 805 | Nov 2025 |

| Qwen 3.5 Plus (news) | -5.3% | -19.1% | 36.7% | 839 | Feb 2026 |

| Qwen 3 Max (news) | -5.8% | -48.0% | 36.3% | 1,835 | Nov 2025 |

| Grok 4.20 Beta (news) | -10.7% | -28.9% | 37.0% | 1,264 | Mar 2026 |

| DeepSeek V3.2 (news) | -17.1% | -32.2% | 42.6% | 2,393 | Nov 2025 |

| MiniMax M2.7 (news) | -17.5% | -20.7% | 42.3% | 1,200 | Mar 2026 |

| Nemotron 3 Super (news) | -22.5% | -37.5% | 37.0% | 1,432 | Mar 2026 |

"News" means the model also reads a real-time news feed. "Price only" means candles and nothing else.

  
\*\*1. Four models were up about 80% at some point. Three gave it back.\*\*

\- Mistral Medium peaked at +117% on 21 August. It is at +14% today.

\- Gemini 3 Pro (price only) peaked at +80% on 9 February. It is at -5%.

\- Qwen 3 Max peaked at +79% on 6 February. It is at -6%.

\- Kimi K2 Thinking peaked at +82% on 7 October and still holds +46%.  


\*\*2. The leader keeps changing.\*\*   
  
Qwen 3 Max led the board on 1 January and on 1 April. Mistral Medium led in mid-July and again in late September. Today's leader, Gemini 3.1 Pro, was third on both of those dates. Back the leader at any of those four dates and you would hold +14% or -6% today.



\*\*3. Win rate tells you nothing.\*\*   
  
Every model wins between 35% and 43% of its trades. The highest win rate on the board, 42.6%, belongs to DeepSeek V3.2, which is at -17%. It also trades the most (2,393 trades) and holds the shortest, 8.5 hours on average.



\*\*4. Fees took most of the profit.\*\*   
  
The 16 accounts started with $160,000 between them and hold $167,500 today: +$7,500 net, after $34,300 of fees. Before fees, the same trades made about $41,800, so fees took about four fifths of it.



\*\*5. They still bet big.\*\*   
  
The median position open right now is 39% of the model's equity (68 positions open as I write). Yet, their size carries no information. Correlation between position size and forward return: 0.007.

What'd be interesting now that we have one year of lookback data, is to check if caping their position size would have made a difference or not. If yes, we could test that from now on.

  
For the curious who wonder how much this have cost so far: $3,470 in API calls over the last 12 months.

Happy to answer any technical question!

comments.body: So when are you going live?

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: the windows make the board hard to read. Gemini 3.1 Pro started in February and Kimi K2 Thinking last November, so part of the ranking is just which months each one got. good to see the clock moved from seconds to 4 hours since your September run. I built my own version of this, Quantradin: you connect an AI and it trades fake money, US stocks and options only. quantradin.com. how does each model compare with just holding the S&P over its own window?

comments.author: Repulsive_Cloud_7435
comments.body:
Great writeup, a full year with fees and no resets is rare. A few questions:



1. How are fees modeled: taker on every fill, or do limit entries get maker rates? With fees eating \~4/5 of gross, that assumption probably decides who ends up green.

2. Do you have gross vs net per model? I'd love to see which ones had a real edge before fees and just traded it away.

3. Any buy-and-hold baseline for the same 5 markets over the same windows? +4.7% combined is hard to judge without it.

4. On the position cap idea: I'd also test a minimum holding time or max trades per day. DeepSeek having the best win rate, the most trades and the shortest holds while sitting at -17% looks like a turnover problem more than a signal problem.



Thanks for sharing the data.

comments.author: Ashimgh
comments.body: What is the flow? What strategy are the models using? or do the models decide the best strategy for themselves?

comments.author: Classic_Television33
comments.body: Interesting results. But it's non-conclusive because you left out the best: Opus 5.5, GPT Sol, Astra, DeepSeek V4/4.1 and the newer Gemini models. DS V3.2 is ancient. No one would go live with that today.
